goal: Bootstrap the Node.js/TypeScript/Express project with an app factory, entry point, and passing smoke test.
scope_summary: Create package.json with all required dependencies (typescript, express, vitest, supertest, and their type packages), tsconfig.json for TS compilation, src/app.ts exporting a createApp factory that returns an Express app without starting a listener, src/index.ts that calls the factory and listens on a port, and tests/app.test.ts verifying the app can be imported and boots without error. Define build and test npm scripts.
planned_changes: Create package.json with typescript, express, vitest, supertest deps and build/test scripts
Create tsconfig.json targeting ES2020/Node with src include and dist outDir
Create src/app.ts exporting a createApp factory returning an Express application
Create src/index.ts importing createApp and starting the server on PORT env or 3000
Create tests/app.test.ts with a smoke test verifying app boots without error
acceptance_checks: package.json has typescript, express, vitest, and supertest dependencies
Express app exported as factory so tests import without starting a listener
src/index.ts starts the server on a port
npm scripts: build, test are defined
Unit test: app.test.ts > 'app boots without error' verifies the app can be imported
commit_message: feat(F001): bootstrap TypeScript/Express project with app factory and smoke test
risks: vitest config may need explicit setup for TypeScript — may require vitest.config.ts or package.json vitest section
Type packages (@types/express, @types/supertest) must be included or TS compilation will fail on import types
tsconfig must exclude tests or use a separate tsconfig.build.json to avoid compiling test files into dist
